source_meta._title: Endermen holding powder snow drop a powder snow bucket when killed

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 20w46a in a newly created vanilla single-player Creative-mode world. Commands/cheats must be enabled, difficulty must not be Peaceful, and the default doMobLoot game rule must remain enabled. Default keyboard and mouse inputs are referenced; use the equivalent configured controls if bindings have been changed.
preconditions: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 20w46a is installed and can be launched from the Minecraft Launcher.
Use a new or disposable world so that unrelated entities and previously dropped items cannot be confused with the summoned Enderman's death drops.
Create the world in Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled.
Set the difficulty to Easy, Normal, or Hard; do not use Peaceful, because hostile entities may be removed.
Leave the doMobLoot game rule at its default value of true so that entity death drops are generated.
Do not load mods, plugins, or datapacks that alter Endermen, entity equipment, combat, or mob drops.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the affected snapshot selected for this reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The title screen displays Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 20w46a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and select a non-Peaceful difficulty such as Normal. Create the world.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON; Difficulty: Normal
steps.success_cue: The player loads into a new Creative-mode world and can open chat commands.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement, inventory input, and chat input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are visible and the player can move without world-loading interruption.

steps.action: Obtain an unenchanted diamond sword for the manual kill. Press E to open the Creative inventory, select the Search Items tab (normally marked by a compass), enter the item name in the search field, and place one Diamond Sword into an empty hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E.
steps.exact_input: diamond sword
steps.success_cue: An unenchanted Diamond Sword is present in one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Move to a level, open location and confirm there are no other Endermen or loose item entities immediately around the player. This keeps the summoned entity and its later drops unambiguous.
steps.success_cue: There is clear ground beside the player where one Enderman can be summoned and visually tracked.

steps.action: Press T, or the configured Open Chat control, to open in-game chat.
steps.exact_input: T
steps.success_cue: The chat command entry field is open and ready for text input.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, capitalization, braces, quotation marks, and NBT, and then press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /summon minecraft:enderman ~ ~ ~ {NoAI:1b,carriedBlockState:{Name:"minecraft:powder_snow"}}
steps.success_cue: The command executes without a syntax error and an Enderman appears at or immediately beside the player's position.

steps.action: Visually identify the newly summoned Enderman. Confirm that it is stationary because of the NoAI tag and that it is visibly carrying a powder snow block. If it spawned inside the player's position, move a few blocks away so the full entity can be targeted.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one stationary Enderman carrying a light-colored powder snow block is visible and reachable by melee attacks.

steps.action: Select the Diamond Sword by pressing the number key corresponding to its hotbar slot or by scrolling to that slot. Approach until the Enderman is within melee range, keep the crosshair centered on its body, and remain on the ground rather than jumping so accidental critical hits do not make the lethal strike less predictable.
steps.exact_input: Select the Diamond Sword hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Diamond Sword is visible in the player's hand and the crosshair is aimed at the Enderman from melee range.

steps.action: Kill the Enderman with direct sword attacks. Left-click once, wait for the attack-cooldown indicator to refill fully, and repeat. Keep the crosshair on this Enderman, do not jump, and do not use commands, fire, environmental damage, or another entity to finish it. As soon as the Enderman receives the lethal hit and begins disappearing, stop attacking and do not move away.
steps.exact_input: Repeated fully charged left-click attacks with the unenchanted Diamond Sword
steps.success_cue: The summoned Enderman has completed its death animation following the final sword hit, and no additional player action has been taken after its death.

stor.handoff_condition: The summoned Enderman carrying powder snow has just been killed by the player's final melee attack. The player has stopped attacking and remains beside the death location; begin observing the generated death drops and any immediate item pickup without performing another command or action.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world type, difficulty, or kill weapon. A new Creative-mode world with cheats, a non-Peaceful difficulty, and an unenchanted Diamond Sword are practical execution choices rather than stated reproduction requirements.

The report says only to kill the Enderman. Manual fully charged sword attacks are used to preserve an ordinary player-caused mob death without introducing an additional kill command or environmental damage source.

The exact number of sword attacks is intentionally not fixed because partially charged or accidental critical attacks can change the count; the trigger is the final attack that actually kills the Enderman.
The summon command is preserved exactly from the report and is used directly in the first listed affected version, 20w46a.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-217524:Baby cat sits and stand up if I just feed her
source_meta._title: Feeding tamed baby wolves and cats causes them to sit down/stand up

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 20w49a in a new single-player world. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled for deterministic setup, then switch to Survival mode before taming and feeding the kitten so the interaction consumes items normally. No particular seed, coordinates, world type, or multiplayer server is specified by the report.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher has a Java Edition installation for snapshot 20w49a.
A mouse or equivalent control is available for the Use Item/Place Block action, which is right-click by default.
The test world permits commands. In a Creative single-player world, commands are available by default.
Use a baby cat, not an adult cat. The report comments explicitly state that the cat variant is reproducible only with a kitten.
Keep at least one Raw Cod after taming so a separate, single feeding interaction can be used as the trigger.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation for snapshot 20w49a and start the game. Do not select the listed fix version 24w11a.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 20w49a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. No specific seed is required because none is provided in the report.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new Creative-mode single-player world and can fly or access the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Move onto an unobstructed solid surface with several blocks of open space around the player. Wait until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on loaded terrain with enough clear space for a kitten to appear two blocks away.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the summon command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The negative Age value creates a baby cat rather than an adult cat.
steps.exact_input: /summon minecraft:cat ~2 ~ ~ {Age:-24000}
steps.success_cue: A visibly small, untamed cat is present approximately two blocks from the player, and no command syntax error is displayed.

steps.action: Press T, enter the give command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This supplies enough Raw Cod for the probabilistic taming attempts and leaves fish available for the final feeding interaction.
steps.exact_input: /give @s minecraft:cod 64
steps.success_cue: A stack of 64 Raw Cod is present in the player's inventory, normally in the first hotbar slot because the inventory was empty.

steps.action: Press T, enter the game-mode command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /gamemode survival
steps.success_cue: The player is in Survival mode; the Survival health and hunger HUD is visible above the hotbar.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing Raw Cod by pressing its corresponding number key, normally 1, or by scrolling until Raw Cod is shown in the player's hand.
steps.success_cue: Raw Cod is visible in the player's main hand and its item name appears briefly above the hotbar.

steps.action: Face the untamed kitten while continuing to hold Raw Cod. Stop moving and avoid sharply turning the camera so the kitten can approach. When it is within interaction reach, place the crosshair on its body and press the Use Item action once, right-click by default. If it remains untamed, allow it to approach again and repeat one right-click at a time until it is tamed. Raw Cod and Raw Salmon are valid cat-taming items. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Turkish_translation/Kedi?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Right-click, repeating only until taming succeeds
steps.success_cue: Taming heart particles have appeared and the kitten now wears a collar, confirming that it belongs to the player.

steps.action: Visually confirm that the tamed cat is still a baby: its body and head should be noticeably smaller than those of an adult cat. If it has become an adult before taming completed, return to step 4 and prepare a fresh kitten; do not continue with an adult cat.
steps.success_cue: A collar-wearing tamed kitten, rather than an adult cat, is present near the player.

steps.action: Put the tamed kitten into a known standing pose without holding fish. Press 2 to select the empty second hotbar slot. Inspect the kitten: if it is sitting, aim at it and right-click once with the empty hand to make it stand; if it is already standing, do not interact with it.
steps.exact_input: 2; if the kitten is sitting, right-click once
steps.success_cue: The selected hand is empty and the tamed kitten is visibly standing on all four legs rather than sitting.

steps.action: Re-select the hotbar slot containing the remaining Raw Cod, normally slot 1. Do not right-click yet.
steps.success_cue: At least one Raw Cod is selected in the player's main hand while the tamed kitten remains standing.

steps.action: Move within normal interaction reach of the tamed kitten and place the crosshair directly over its body. Stop moving and ensure no other cat, mob, or block is under the crosshair.
steps.success_cue: The standing, collar-wearing kitten is directly under the crosshair, Raw Cod is selected, and the player is close enough to use the fish on it.

steps.action: Press the Use Item action exactly once while aiming at the tamed standing kitten, right-click by default. Do not issue a second interaction or change the kitten's pose afterward; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once
steps.success_cue: A single feeding/use interaction has just been issued to the tamed baby cat while Raw Cod was selected.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just right-clicked the standing, tamed kitten exactly once with Raw Cod in the main hand. No follow-up interaction has been performed; begin observing the kitten's state and the immediate interaction feedback.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode with cheats is used only to make setup deterministic, followed by Survival mode for taming and the trigger interaction.
The kitten summon command and Raw Cod give command are operational additions; neither exact command appears in the Mojira report.

The web source confirms Raw Cod or Raw Salmon as appropriate cat-taming and feeding items, but an archival page explicitly documenting the full 20w49a summon command was not available. The supplied summon syntax is a practical version-compatible implementation choice.

The report title and description also identify tamed baby wolves fed meat, but the formal Steps to Reproduce describe only a kitten. This plan follows that formal kitten path and does not add a second wolf trigger.
Comment 11 mentions confirmation in 23w42a, but 23w42a is not present in the report's Affects versions field and therefore has not been added to affected_versions.

source_meta.attachment filenames: Minecraft 22w12a Warden Despawning.mp4; Minecraft 22w15a - Multiplayer Warden Despawning.mp4; Minecraft 22w18a - Singleplayer 2022-05-06 09-11-57_Trim.mp4; Minecraft 22w18a Warden Despawns.mp4; screenshot-1.png

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w12a in a new single-player world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled, a non-Peaceful difficulty such as Normal, and an open area with solid level ground. A Superflat world is recommended as a practical way to provide unobstructed terrain. Set Simulation Distance to at least 10 chunks so the Warden's chunk can continue ticking when the player is 130 blocks away.
preconditions: Launch the game using Java Edition snapshot 22w12a, the first version listed as affected.
Use a new single-player world so no second player remains close enough to affect distance-based mob despawning.
Enable commands when creating the world. Creative mode is recommended so the Warden cannot interrupt command entry by killing the player.
Set the difficulty to Normal or another non-Peaceful difficulty.
Set Simulation Distance to 10 chunks or greater before summoning the Warden.
Use an open location with solid, level ground and at least three blocks of vertical clearance.
Ensure there is no existing Warden near the test location.
Perform the summon and teleport sequence promptly; do not intentionally wait for the Warden's ordinary inactivity-based digging sequence.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for snapshot 22w12a, start it, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition main menu is displayed and identifies the running version as 22w12a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, enable commands or Allow Cheats, and create the world. A Superflat world may be selected under More World Options to provide a simple open test area.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a new single-player Creative world and can open chat and execute commands.

steps.action: Open the pause menu with Esc, open Options, and set Difficulty to Normal if the world is currently on Peaceful.
steps.success_cue: The displayed difficulty is Normal or another non-Peaceful setting.

steps.action: From Options, open Video Settings and set Simulation Distance to at least 10 chunks. Return to the game after applying the setting.
steps.success_cue: Simulation Distance is 10 chunks or greater and the player has returned to normal gameplay.

steps.action: Wait until the world finishes loading, then stand on solid, level ground in an open area. Do not stand in water, over a drop, or beside a hazard that could move or damage the Warden while the player is away.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are rendered, movement responds normally, and there is sufficient unobstructed space for a Warden at the player's position.

steps.action: Press T, or the rebound Open Chat control, to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat command-entry field is active.

steps.action: Enter the summon command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not add NBT such as PersistenceRequired, NoAI, or a custom name.
steps.exact_input: /summon minecraft:warden ~ ~ ~
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red syntax error and one Warden is present at the player's current location.

steps.action: As soon as the Warden has appeared, press T to open chat again. Avoid walking away manually or spending time interacting with the Warden.
steps.success_cue: Chat is open while the player is still at the location where the Warden was summoned.

steps.action: Enter the report's first teleport command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The relative X coordinate moves the player 130 blocks in the negative X direction; the final two arguments set yaw to -90 and pitch to 0.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and the player is now 130 blocks west of the Warden's summon location, facing at yaw -90 with level pitch.

steps.action: Allow approximately one second of normal game time to pass so the teleport completes and entities receive game ticks. Do not remain away for an extended period.
steps.success_cue: Player movement and commands respond normally at the distant location; no more than a brief interval has elapsed.

steps.action: Press T to open chat while remaining at the distant location.
steps.success_cue: The chat command-entry field is active and the player has not moved manually from the teleported position.

steps.action: Enter the report's return teleport command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This reverses the earlier relative X displacement and returns the player to the Warden's summon location.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and the player is back at the original summon coordinates, facing at yaw -90 with level pitch.

steps.action: Close chat if it remains visible and wait only until the chunks around the original location have rendered and camera movement responds normally. Do not perform any additional commands, summon another Warden, or leave the location.
steps.success_cue: The player is at the original Warden summon location, surrounding terrain is rendered, and the scene is ready for immediate inspection without yet evaluating the bug outcome.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has crossed to 130 blocks from the summoned Warden in step 9, briefly allowed entity ticking, and has now returned to the exact summon location in step 12. The original area is rendered and ready for the observation subsystem to inspect the Warden's state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, terrain type, game mode, difficulty, or single-player versus multiplayer requirement. A new single-player Creative Superflat world on Normal difficulty is selected as the simplest controlled implementation.

The report says only “Summon a warden” and does not provide an exact summon command. The plan uses `/summon minecraft:warden ~ ~ ~` without NBT as the deterministic implementation; adding persistence-related NBT would alter the reported test condition.
The report does not specify Simulation Distance. At least 10 chunks is selected as a practical safeguard so the original location can remain entity-ticking at a 130-block separation.

The report also describes a randomized variant at a distance of 48 blocks. That variant is not used because the supplied 130-block path is shorter and intended to reproduce immediately rather than depend on random despawn timing.

22w15a appears in both the report's affected-version list and fix-version list. It is retained in affected_versions exactly as supplied, while 22w12a remains the recommended version because it is the first listed affected version.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MCPE-152559:Frogs lay eggs on Flowing Water
source_meta._title: Frogs can lay spawn on flowing water

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 22w15a in a single-player Creative-mode world with commands/cheats enabled. A flat, open building area is recommended; the report does not require a particular seed, biome, coordinate, difficulty, server, or multiplayer configuration.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version 22w15a rather than the listed fix version 22w24a.
Create or load a Creative-mode world with commands enabled so the two frogs can be summoned deterministically.
Have solid building blocks, transparent blocks such as glass, one Water Bucket, and at least two Slimeballs available from the Creative inventory.
The test structure must expose exactly one flowing-water cell with air directly above it and dry land directly adjacent to it.
The water source feeding the flowing-water cell must have a solid block directly above it so that the source itself is not another eligible frogspawn location.
The frog enclosure must be closed, including a roof, because frogs can jump high enough to escape ordinary short walls.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation using the exact Java Edition snapshot 22w15a, then launch it. Do not use 22w24a because that is listed as a fix version rather than an affected version.
steps.exact_input: Version: 22w15a
steps.success_cue: The lower-left portion of the Minecraft title screen identifies the running version as 22w15a.

steps.action: From the title screen, create a new single-player test world. Set Game Mode to Creative, enable commands/cheats, and use a Superflat world if available to provide an unobstructed building area. The Superflat choice is only an execution convenience and is not asserted by the report.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> World Type: Superflat -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player loads into a Creative-mode world, can fly, and has access to commands.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory action, whose default key is E. Obtain a stack of solid blocks, a stack of glass or another transparent building block, one Water Bucket, and at least two Slimeballs. Place the water bucket and slimeballs in hotbar slots; the hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: E; collect solid blocks, glass, Water Bucket, and at least 2 Slimeballs
steps.success_cue: The required building materials, Water Bucket, and Slimeballs are visible in the inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Choose a flat, unobstructed location and define a floor level. Build a solid horizontal floor at least 5 blocks by 5 blocks. Keep the area above the floor clear for the enclosure.
steps.exact_input: Build a 5x5 solid floor
steps.success_cue: A continuous 5x5 floor exists with open space above it.

steps.action: Choose one side of the floor as the north side. At the middle of that side, remove the edge floor block. Designate the resulting empty floor-level cell as the target cell. Leave the next floor block toward the center of the enclosure intact so a frog can stand on that dry block directly adjacent to the target cell.
steps.exact_input: Remove the center block of the chosen floor edge
steps.success_cue: The target cell is empty at floor level, has a solid support block beneath it, and is directly adjacent to an intact dry floor block on its interior side.

steps.action: Remove or leave empty one additional floor-level cell immediately outward from the target cell, in a straight line away from the enclosure. Designate this outer cell as the source cell. Ensure both the target cell and source cell have solid blocks directly beneath them.
steps.exact_input: Create a second empty floor-level cell directly outside the target cell
steps.success_cue: The source and target form a straight two-cell channel at floor level, with the target adjacent to the dry enclosure floor and the source immediately beyond the target.

steps.action: At floor level, place solid containment blocks along both sides of the two-cell channel and beyond the outer end of the source cell. These blocks must prevent water from spreading sideways or farther outward. Do not place a block between the source and target cells.
steps.exact_input: Contain both sides and the outer end of the 1x2 channel with solid blocks
steps.success_cue: The only open horizontal path out of the source cell leads into the target cell, and the target's interior neighbor is the intact dry floor block.

steps.action: Place a solid block exactly one block above the source cell. Leave the block exactly one block above the target cell as air. This prevents the covered source from being an eligible laying location while preserving the exposed flowing-water target.
steps.exact_input: Cover source cell at source Y+1; leave target Y+1 empty
steps.success_cue: The source cell is directly covered by a solid block, while the target cell has unobstructed air directly above it.

steps.action: Build transparent perimeter walls around the 5x5 test floor and connect them to the channel containment blocks. Make the interior walls at least two blocks tall above floor level. Leave one temporary opening large enough for the player to enter.
steps.exact_input: Build enclosure walls 2 blocks above floor level, leaving one temporary entrance
steps.success_cue: The land area and target cell are surrounded by walls except for the temporary player entrance.

steps.action: Add a complete roof at least three blocks above floor level, using glass where visibility is useful. The roof must leave two blocks of interior air above the dry floor and must not fill the air block directly above the target water cell. Enter the enclosure through the temporary opening and then close that opening with the same wall material.
steps.exact_input: Roof at floor Y+3; enter enclosure; close temporary entrance
steps.success_cue: The player is inside a fully closed chamber, the dry floor has usable headroom, and the target cell still has air immediately above it.

steps.action: Select the Water Bucket in the active hotbar slot. Use the bucket once on the source cell, using the Use Item action whose default input is right-click. Do not place water directly into the target cell.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the source cell once with the Water Bucket
steps.success_cue: One source block occupies the covered source cell and water has spread from it into the exposed target cell.

steps.action: Verify the water configuration before introducing frogs. The outer source cell must be the only cell where a bucket was emptied; the exposed target cell must contain water solely because water spread into it from the source. Confirm that the target has air directly above it and dry land immediately beside it.
steps.success_cue: The uncovered target is a flowing-water cell fed by the covered source, with an adjacent dry floor block available for a frog to stand on.

steps.action: Stand near the center of the enclosed dry floor. Open chat with the default T key, enter the exact summon command including the leading slash, and press Enter to summon the first frog one block to one side of the player.
steps.exact_input: /summon minecraft:frog ~1 ~ ~
steps.success_cue: A living frog is visible inside the enclosure and the command does not report a syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Open chat again, enter the second exact summon command including the leading slash, and press Enter to summon another frog on the other side of the player.
steps.exact_input: /summon minecraft:frog ~-1 ~ ~
steps.success_cue: Exactly two living frogs are present inside the closed enclosure.

steps.action: Select the Slimeball in the active hotbar slot. Aim the crosshair at the first frog and use the Slimeball once with the Use Item action, whose default input is right-click. Avoid clicking the same frog a second time.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the first frog once with a Slimeball
steps.success_cue: Heart particles appear above the first frog, indicating that it has entered love mode.

steps.action: While still holding the Slimeball, aim at the second frog and use the Slimeball once with right-click.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the second frog once with a Slimeball
steps.success_cue: Heart particles appear above the second frog and the two frogs begin moving toward each other to mate.

steps.action: Wait without damaging or separating the frogs until the mating interaction completes. Keep the chamber closed and do not place, remove, or update blocks around the water channel.
steps.success_cue: The mating heart-particle sequence ends, both frogs remain inside the chamber, and one frog is ready to perform its post-mating lay-spawn behavior.

steps.action: Stop holding the Slimeball so the frogs are not tempted toward the player. Select an empty hotbar slot or a non-slimeball item, move away from the target-water side, and remain still while keeping the target area visible.
steps.exact_input: Select an empty or non-Slimeball hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: No Slimeball is held in the player's hand, and the frogs can navigate toward the water without following the player.

steps.action: Wait for the post-mating frog to approach the dry floor block adjacent to the uncovered flowing-water target and complete its lay-spawn action. Do not interact with the frog, water, or nearby blocks during this wait. As soon as the laying action and associated sound complete, stop all player input and hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The frog has just completed its lay-spawn action beside the uncovered flowing-water target; no subsequent block update has been intentionally caused.

stor.handoff_condition: The post-mating frog has just completed its lay-spawn action beside the single exposed flowing-water cell. Begin observation of the target cell immediately, before the player places, removes, touches, or otherwise updates any nearby block.
uncertainties: The supplied report refers to setup.png, but the attachment image itself is not included in the supplied report text. The described 5x5 enclosure and covered-source/flowing-target channel are a functional reconstruction rather than a claim that they exactly match the attachment's dimensions or materials.

The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, biome, world type, game mode, or difficulty. Creative mode with commands and an optional Superflat world was selected solely to make the reproduction deterministic and quick.
The report says to summon two frogs but does not provide an exact command. The namespaced Java Edition command '/summon minecraft:frog' is used as the deterministic operational implementation.

The report provides no fixed amount of time for the pregnant frog to approach water. Step 19 therefore uses the frog's completed lay-spawn action and sound as the observable readiness condition rather than prescribing an unsupported timer.

The reconstruction deliberately covers the water source and exposes only the flowing target so that the frog cannot select an uncovered source-water cell instead. This isolation detail is inferred from the behavior being tested rather than explicitly stated in the written report.

source_meta._title: Horse temporarily stuck in jump animation if dismounted

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition using the exact affected version Minecraft 1.9 Pre-Release 1. Use a single-player Creative-mode world as a deterministic way to obtain a horse and saddle. Perform the trigger on unobstructed, level ground with enough room for the horse to jump and land. The report does not require multiplayer, a particular seed, commands, or cheats.
preconditions: The exact Minecraft Java Edition version Minecraft 1.9 Pre-Release 1 is installed and launchable.
Default controls are assumed: E opens the inventory, Space is Jump, and Left Shift is Sneak/Dismount. If controls are rebound, use the keys assigned to those actions instead.
A mouse or equivalent input is available for right-click interactions.
The world contains an unobstructed patch of level, solid ground with no low ceiling or nearby drop that could interfere with the horse's jump or landing.
The reproduction requires an adult horse that has been tamed and equipped with a saddle before the timing-sensitive trigger is attempted.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Java Edition installation for the first listed affected version. Do not use either listed fix version for this reproduction.
steps.exact_input: Select and launch "Minecraft 1.9 Pre-Release 1" in the Minecraft Launcher.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu has loaded and displays the selected affected version.

steps.action: Create a single-player Creative-mode world. No particular seed or world-generation setting is required. After entering the world, wait for nearby terrain to render and for movement and inventory input to respond normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded Creative-mode world and can move without chunk-loading interruption.

steps.action: Locate an unobstructed area of level, solid ground. Move away from trees, walls, pits, water, and low overhead blocks so the horse will have room to jump and land normally.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D and the mouse to move to and inspect a clear area.
steps.success_cue: Several blocks of flat, solid ground are clear around the player, including open air above the intended horse position.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and obtain a Horse Spawn Egg. Use the Search Items tab if necessary, then place the spawn egg into an available hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: Press E; select Search Items; search for "horse"; move the Horse Spawn Egg to the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: A Horse Spawn Egg is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory is still open, obtain a Saddle and place it into another available hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: In Search Items, search for "saddle"; move the Saddle to the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: Both a Horse Spawn Egg and a Saddle are present in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory, select the Horse Spawn Egg in the hotbar, aim at the clear ground, and use the egg to spawn a horse. Use an adult horse; if the spawned entity is not a suitable adult horse, spawn another on the clear ground and use the adult horse.
steps.exact_input: Press E to close the inventory; select the Horse Spawn Egg with the corresponding number key or mouse wheel; right-click the ground.
steps.success_cue: An adult horse is standing on the unobstructed ground near the player.

steps.action: Prepare to tame the horse without accidentally using an item on it. Select an empty hotbar slot so the player's hand is empty.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key for an empty hotbar slot or scroll to one.
steps.success_cue: The active hotbar slot is empty and the player's hand contains no item.

steps.action: Mount the adult horse by aiming the crosshair at its body and using the interaction control.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the horse with an empty hand.
steps.success_cue: The viewpoint is positioned on the horse, indicating that the player has mounted it.

steps.action: Complete the taming process. If the untamed horse throws the player off, approach it and right-click it with an empty hand again. Repeat only until the horse accepts the rider and the taming heart particles appear.
steps.exact_input: After each forced dismount, right-click the horse again with an empty hand.
steps.success_cue: Heart particles have appeared and the horse no longer immediately throws the player off, confirming that it is tamed.

steps.action: While mounted on the tamed horse, open the horse inventory. This interface includes the player's inventory and the horse's equipment slots.
steps.exact_input: Press E while mounted.
steps.success_cue: The horse inventory interface is open and its saddle equipment slot is visible.

steps.action: Equip the horse with the Saddle obtained earlier. Move the Saddle from the hotbar or player inventory into the horse's saddle equipment slot.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the Saddle, then left-click the horse's saddle slot.
steps.success_cue: The Saddle is displayed in the horse's saddle slot and appears on the horse model.

steps.action: Close the horse inventory. If closing the interface leaves the player mounted, remain mounted. If the player is not mounted, aim at the saddled horse and right-click it to start riding.
steps.exact_input: Press E to close the interface; if necessary, right-click the saddled horse.
steps.success_cue: The player is riding the tamed, saddled horse and the horse can be controlled by the player.

steps.action: Position the mounted horse on the prepared level ground and bring it to a complete stop. Ensure there is still open space above and around it.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D as needed, then release all movement keys.
steps.success_cue: The mounted horse is stationary on level, solid ground with an unobstructed landing area.

steps.action: Begin charging a horse jump by pressing and holding the Jump control. Continue holding until the horse jump-charge meter has visibly risen; a maximum-strength charge is not required.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold Space.
steps.success_cue: The horse jump-charge meter is visible and has accumulated charge while the player remains mounted.

steps.action: Trigger the test by releasing the Jump control and pressing the Dismount control at the same moment. For automated input, issue the Space key-up event and Left Shift key-down event in the same client frame or simulation tick. Release Left Shift after the player has dismounted.
steps.exact_input: Release Space and press Left Shift simultaneously; then release Left Shift once dismounted.
steps.success_cue: The charged jump has been released and the player has dismounted at the start of the horse's jump, with the horse beginning the jump or already airborne.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just released the charged horse jump and dismounted in the same moment, while the horse is beginning the jump or is airborne above the prepared level ground. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately so it can watch the horse through its landing and subsequent movement.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required game mode, world seed, world type, or multiplayer environment. Creative-mode single player is used only as a practical, deterministic resource-acquisition setup.
Manual horse taming can require a variable number of mounting attempts. Continue only until heart particles confirm that the adult horse is tamed.
The trigger is timing-sensitive. The report requires releasing Space and pressing Shift at the same time; inputs separated across multiple client frames may not reproduce the intended condition.
The plan uses a Horse Spawn Egg because the report does not provide a seed, coordinates, or command for locating a horse. This is a setup convenience rather than a reported reproduction requirement.
